args.final_thought:
I need to finalize with a fine-trace JSON array. Based on my analysis, the vulnerability is the format 4 `glyphIdArrayLength` off-by-one in `hb-ot-cmap-table.hh`. The `glyphIdArrayLength` is computed as `(subtable->length - 16 - 8*segCount)/2`, but the `glyphIdArray` actually starts at byte offset `16 + 8*segCount + 2` (including the reservedPad). This makes `glyphIdArrayLength` 1 more than the actual count, allowing a read of `glyphIdArray[glyphIdArrayLength-1]` at byte offset `length`, which can be past the end of the heap allocation when the subtable is at the end of the blob.

```json
[
  {"step": 1, "file": "test/fuzzing/hb-subset-get-codepoints-fuzzer.cc", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 12, "var": "data", "code": "hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);", "note": "Attacker-controlled raw font bytes are wrapped in an hb_blob_t; the blob is the heap allocation that later reads may overrun."},
  {"step": 2, "file": "test/fuzzing/hb-subset-get-codepoints-fuzzer.cc", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 13, "var": "face", "code": "hb_face_t *face = hb_face_create (blob, 0);", "note": "A face is created from the blob; the SFNT table directory is parsed and the cmap table is located."},
  {"step": 3, "file": "test/fuzzing/hb-subset-get-codepoints-fuzzer.cc", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 16, "var": "output", "code": "hb_face_collect_unicodes (face, output);", "note": "Triggers cmap table parsing and the collect_unicodes path on the attacker-controlled cmap subtable."},
  {"step": 4, "file": "src/hb-face.cc", "function": "hb_face_collect_unicodes", "line": 536, "var": "face", "code": "hb_ot_face_data (face)->cmap->collect_unicodes (out);", "note": "Dispatches to the cmap accelerator's collect_unicodes, which selects the best subtable (format 4)."},
  {"step": 5, "file": "src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh", "function": "CmapSubtableFormat4::accelerator_t::init", "line": 531, "var": "glyphIdArrayLength", "code": "glyphIdArrayLength = (subtable->length - 16 - 8 * segCount) / 2;", "note": "glyphIdArrayLength is computed from the attacker-controlled subtable->length field, but glyphIdArray actually starts at byte offset 16+8*segCount+2 (after reservedPad), so glyphIdArrayLength is 1 more than the real number of entries."},
  {"step": 6, "file": "src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh", "function": "CmapSubtableFormat4::accelerator_t::init", "line": 534, "var": "glyphIdArray", "code": "glyphIdArray = idRangeOffset + segCount;", "note": "glyphIdArray points to the start of the glyph index array; because of the reservedPad the array is 2 bytes later than the length formula assumes."},
  {"step": 7, "file": "src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh", "function": "CmapSubtableFormat4::accelerator_t::collect_unicodes", "line": 622, "var": "index", "code": "unsigned int index = rangeOffset / 2 + (codepoint - this->startCount[i]) + i - this->segCount;", "note": "For a crafted idRangeOffset, index is computed to equal glyphIdArrayLength-1, the last (out-of-bounds) element the off-by-one permits."},
  {"step": 8, "file": "src/hb-ot-cmap-table.hh", "function": "CmapSubtableFormat4::accelerator_t::collect_unicodes", "line": 624, "var": "gid", "code": "hb_codepoint_t gid = this->glyphIdArray[index];", "note": "Reads glyphIdArray[glyphIdArrayLength-1] at byte offset subtable->length; when the subtable sits at the end of the blob this reads past the heap allocation, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ."}
]
```
